# 📚 Bookmark App

A full-stack bookmarking service built for the **Capstone Project: Full-Stack Vibe-Coded Service with GitHub CI/CD & Database**. Users can register, log in, and manage a personal collection of bookmarks — all backed by a live PostgreSQL database, secured against common web vulnerabilities, tested automatically, and deployed to the public internet through a CI/CD pipeline.

- **Live App (Frontend):** https://bookmark-app-two-lake.vercel.app
- **Live API (Backend):** https://bookmark-app-production-98c0.up.railway.app
- **GitHub Repository:** https://github.com/zahraasamyelnaggar-source/bookmark-app

## Architecture & SDLC Overview

This project follows a classic **3-tier architecture**:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[Frontend<br/>HTML/CSS/JS<br/>Vercel] -->|HTTPS/REST| B[Backend API<br/>Express + Prisma<br/>Railway]
    B -->|SQL over TLS| C[(PostgreSQL Database<br/>Neon)]
    D[GitHub Repository] -->|Push to main| E[GitHub Actions CI/CD]
    E -->|Run tests + secret scan| E
    E -->|Auto-deploy| B
    E -->|Auto-deploy| A
```

**Tier breakdown:**
- **Frontend tier** — a static HTML/CSS/JavaScript single-page app, hosted on Vercel. Talks to the backend exclusively via `fetch()` calls to the REST API.
- **Backend / API tier** — a Node.js + Express REST API, hosted on Railway. Handles authentication (JWT), input validation, and all bookmark CRUD logic. Uses Prisma as the ORM layer to talk to the database.
- **Database tier** — a live, serverless PostgreSQL database hosted on Neon, storing users, bookmarks, and tags.

**SDLC process followed:**
1. **Planning** — defined the app scope (a bookmarking service), designed the 3-tier architecture and the relational schema (`users`, `bookmarks`, `tags`) before writing any code.
2. **Environment setup** — provisioned a live Neon Postgres database and a GitHub repository with a proper `.gitignore` and feature-branch workflow from the start.
3. **Vibe-coded implementation** — built the backend (auth, CRUD, ownership checks) and frontend (login/register, bookmark management UI) with AI assistance, testing each piece against the real, live database as it was built rather than against mocks.
4. **Refactoring & review** — every AI-generated issue (malformed environment variables, an npm dependency bug, credential formatting mistakes) was caught, fixed, and logged in [`REFACTORING_LOG.md`](./REFACTORING_LOG.md) as it happened.
5. **Security pass** — added password hashing (bcrypt), parameterized queries (via Prisma), input validation (express-validator), and ownership checks on every mutating endpoint.
6. **Automated testing** — wrote Jest + Supertest test suites covering both auth and bookmarks routes, reaching 85.85% coverage.
7. **CI/CD** — built a GitHub Actions pipeline that installs dependencies, generates the Prisma client, runs the full test suite against the live database, and scans for leaked secrets on every push.
8. **Deployment** — deployed the backend to Railway and the frontend to Vercel, both connected to the same live Neon database, and verified the full stack end-to-end in production.

## Tech Stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Frontend | HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript |
| Backend | Node.js, Express |
| ORM / Database Layer | Prisma |
| Database | PostgreSQL (hosted on Neon) |
| Authentication | JWT (jsonwebtoken), bcryptjs for password hashing |
| Validation | express-validator |
| Testing | Jest, Supertest |
| CI/CD | GitHub Actions, Gitleaks (secret scanning) |
| Hosting | Railway (backend), Vercel (frontend) |

---

## Features

- User registration and login with hashed passwords and JWT-based authentication
- Create, read, update, and delete personal bookmarks
- Each bookmark stores a URL, title, and optional description
- Ownership enforcement — users can only view, edit, or delete their own bookmarks
- Input validation on every endpoint (valid email, valid URL, required fields)
- Fully responsive, dependency-free frontend

## Security

This project addresses the following items from the OWASP Top 10:

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| SQL Injection | All database queries go through Prisma's parameterized query builder — no raw string concatenation is used anywhere in the codebase. |
| Broken Authentication | Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (never stored in plaintext) before being saved; JWTs are used for stateless session authentication with a 7-day expiry. |
| Sensitive Data Exposure | The `.env` file (containing the real database URL and JWT secret) is excluded via `.gitignore` and was never committed to the repository. Only `.env.example`, containing placeholder values, is tracked. |
| Broken Access Control | Every bookmark update/delete route verifies that `bookmark.userId` matches the authenticated user's ID before allowing the action — enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI. Automated tests specifically verify that one user cannot delete or modify another user's bookmarks. |
| Injection via Unvalidated Input | All incoming request bodies are validated using `express-validator` (valid email format, minimum password length, valid URL format, required fields) before touching the database. |
| Security Misconfiguration | CORS is explicitly configured; error responses do not leak stack traces or internal implementation details to the client. |
| Secrets in Source Control | The CI/CD pipeline runs Gitleaks on every push to automatically scan for and flag any accidentally committed credentials. |

## Testing

The backend is covered by an automated Jest + Supertest test suite covering both the authentication and bookmarks routes.

**Results:**
- **17 tests, all passing**
- **85.85% overall statement coverage** (exceeding the 80% requirement)
- 96.15% branch coverage, 100% function coverage

**What's tested:**
- User registration (success, invalid email, short password, duplicate email)
- User login (success, wrong password, nonexistent user)
- Bookmark creation (success, invalid URL rejected)
- Bookmark listing (scoped to the authenticated user only)
- Bookmark updates (owner succeeds, non-owner is rejected with 403, nonexistent bookmark returns 404)
- Bookmark deletion (owner succeeds, non-owner is rejected with 403, nonexistent bookmark returns 404)
- Unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401 on protected routes

Run the tests locally with:
```bash
cd backend
npm test
```

---

## CI/CD Pipeline

Defined in [`.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml`](.github/workflows/ci-cd.yml). On every push or pull request to `main`, the pipeline automatically:

1. Checks out the repository
2. Sets up Node.js 20
3. Installs backend dependencies (`npm ci`)
4. Generates the Prisma Client
5. Runs the full test suite with coverage against the live database, using credentials stored securely as GitHub Actions secrets (`DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_SECRET`) — never hardcoded in the workflow file
6. Scans the entire repository for leaked secrets using Gitleaks

## Deployment

| Service | Platform | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Backend | [Railway](https://railway.app) | Hosts the Express API, connected to the live Neon database via environment variables |
| Frontend | [Vercel](https://vercel.com) | Hosts the static frontend, configured to call the live Railway backend URL |
| Database | [Neon](https://neon.tech) | Serverless PostgreSQL, free tier |

Both deployments are connected to the `main` branch of the GitHub repository and can be configured to redeploy automatically on every push.

## Local Setup Instructions

### Prerequisites
- Node.js (v18+)
- A PostgreSQL database (e.g., a free [Neon](https://neon.tech) project)

### Backend
```bash
cd backend
npm install
```

Create a `backend/.env` file (see `backend/.env.example` for the required format):
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host/dbname
JWT_SECRET=your-own-random-secret
PORT=3000
```

Push the schema to your database and start the server:
```bash
npx prisma db push
node src/index.js
```

The API will be running at `http://localhost:3000`.

### Frontend
Open `frontend/index.html` directly in a browser, or serve it with any static file server. Update the `API_URL` constant at the top of `frontend/app.js` to point at your backend if not running on `localhost:3000`.

## API Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Auth Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/auth/register` | No | Register a new user |
| POST | `/api/auth/login` | No | Log in and receive a JWT |
| GET | `/api/bookmarks` | Yes | List the authenticated user's bookmarks |
| POST | `/api/bookmarks` | Yes | Create a new bookmark |
| PUT | `/api/bookmarks/:id` | Yes | Update a bookmark (must be the owner) |
| DELETE | `/api/bookmarks/:id` | Yes | Delete a bookmark (must be the owner) |

Protected routes require an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
